source_text:
ἑτέρα κάτωθεν ὡς ἀποδέδεικται, οὕτως καὶ ἡμῖν ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ ὀργὴ θεοῦ ἐστίν, ἑτέρα
δὲ ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ μὲν οὐ θεοῦ δέ; εἰ δὲ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ὁ θεὸς διὰ τῶν ἐν τῷ φυσικῷ
λόγῳ ἀφορμῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐφανέρωσεν, καὶ τὸ γνωστὸν ἑαυτοῦ ὡς ἕκαστος
κεχώρηκεν ὅτε τὸν λόγον συμπεπλήρωκεν, δηλονότι ἀναγ καῖον ἔσται διὰ πάντα τὰ
ἀσεβῶς γεγενημένα καὶ ἀδίκως πεπραγμένα, τοῖσδε μὲν πλείονα τοῖσδε δὲ ἐλάττονα,
κατὰ ἀναλογίαν ἐλθεῖν τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῆς ὀργῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ. 6 ii 7–9
τοῖς μὲν καθ' ὑπομονὴν ἔργου ἀγαθοῦ δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ ἀφθαρσίαν ζητοῦσι ζωὴν
αἰώνιον· τοῖς δὲ ἐξ ἐριθείας καὶ ἀπειθοῦσι μὲν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πει θομένοις δὲ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ
θυμὸς καὶ ὀργὴ θλίψις καὶ στενοχωρία ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ψυχὴν ἀνθρώπου τοῦ
κατεργαζομένου τὸ κακὸν Ἰουδαίου τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνος. ὀργὴ δέ ἐστιν ὁ
ἑπόμενος τοῖς ἁμαρτάνουσιν ἐπὶ τιμωρίᾳ πόνος· θυμὸν δὲ ὁρίζονται ὀργὴν
ἀναθυμιωμένην καὶ διοιδαίνουσαν· οὗτος δὲ ὁ θυμὸς ἔργον ἔχει τὸ ἐλέγχειν, ἡνίκα
ἂν διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας πάσχων τινά, ἤτοι τῆς συνειδήσεως αὐτῶν πληττομένης ἢ
ἀκολουθούντων ἐπιπόνων τινῶν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ. ἀλλὰ καὶ θλίψις ἕπεται τοῖς τοιούτοις
οὐχ ἡ ὑπομονὴν κατεργαζομένη, οὐδὲ εἰ νῆστις ὢν καυχήσεται, ἀλλ' εἰ συνέζευκται
στενοχωρίᾳ. οὐκ ἂν δέ τις ἐστενοχωρήθη εἰ πεποιήκει τις αὑτῷ ἀπὸ οφία πλάτο
καρδία καὶ ἤκουσε τοῦ ἀποστόλου λέγοντος πλατύνθητε καὶ ὑμεῖ . συνάγειν γὰρ
εἴωθεν καὶ στενοῦν τὴν ψυχὴν τὰ κακά, ὡς τὸν διάβολον ὡς ἐν ὀπῇ κατὰ τὸν ὄφιν
ἐμφωλεύειν. 7 ii 10, 11 δόξα καὶ τιμὴ καὶ εἰρήνη παντὶ τῷ ἐργαζομένῳ τὸ ἀγαθόν,
Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι· οὐ γάρ ἐστιν προσωποληψία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ. ὁ τοίνυν
ἐργαζόμενος τὸ ἀγαθὸν καὶ τίμιον ἑαυτὸν ἀποφαίνων τιμὴν λήψεται, διὰ τῆς
μετανοίας ἀναβαίνων, ἐξ ἧς ἐξέπεσεν ὁμοιωθεὶ τοῖ κτήνε ι τοῖ ἀνοήτοι · καὶ τὰ
ἀφθαρσίας ἄξια πράγματα νοήσας ἐγείρεται ἐν δόξῃ εἰς αἰώνιον ζωήν· καὶ ἐν εἰρήνῃ
δέ ἐστι πᾶς ὁ ἀπερίσπαστος καὶ μὴ περιελκόμενος ὑπό τινος ἄλλο τι νοεῖν ἢ ποιεῖν
παρὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν, κατὰ τὸ καὶ ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ θεοῦ φρουρή ει τὰ καρδία ὑμῶν καὶ
τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν ἐν Χρι τῷ Ἰη οῦ, καὶ εἰρήνη ὑμῖν πληθυνθείη, καὶ τὸ εἰρήνην τὴν
ἐμὴν δίδωμι ὑμῖν· φησὶν δὲ καὶ ὁ προφήτης πλῆθο ἔσεσθαι εἰρήνη ἐν τῇ ἐπιδημίᾳ
τοῦ κυρίου ἕω ἀνταναιρεθῇ ἡ ελήνη, ἵνα μηκέτι νόθον ὑπάρχῃ φῶς καὶ νυκτερινόν.
8 ii 12, 13 ὅσοι γὰρ ἀνόμως ἥμαρτον ἀνόμως καὶ ἀπολοῦνται· καὶ ὅσοι ἐν νόμῳ
ἥμαρτον διὰ νόμου κριθήσονται· οὐ γὰρ οἱ ἀκροαταὶ τοῦ νόμου δίκαιοι παρὰ τῷ θεῷ,
ἀλλ' οἱ ποιηταὶ τοῦ νόμου δικαιωθήσονται. κριθῆναι μέν ἐστι κατὰ νόμον καὶ διὰ
νόμου· τὸ δὲ ἀπολέσθαι οὐκ ἐπιδέχεται νόμον· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἄλλος τις αὐτοὺς ἀπολεῖ, ἵνα
κρίνῃ αὐτοὺς νόμῳ ἀπωλείας, ἀλλ' ἔχεται τοῖς ἀνόμως ἁμαρτήσασιν ἀπώλεια· ὅσοι
δὲ ἐν νόμῳ ἥμαρτον μὴ πάνυ ἀποστατοῦντες αὐτοῦ ἀλλ' ἤτοι παρορῶντες ἢ καὶ
νικώμενοι, μετὰ τοῦ προτίθεσθαι κατὰ νόμον ζῇν, οὗτοι δι' αὐτοῦ τοῦ νόμου
κριθήσονται. 9 ii 15, 16 συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ
ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων, ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ὅτε κρινεῖ
ὁ θεὸς τὰ κρυπτὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. [ἢ καὶ
οὕτως·] κρινεῖ ὁ θεὸς κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον· ὅπερ εὐαγγέλιον Παύλου ἐστιν, καὶ τῶν
παραπλησίων ἐκείνῳ καὶ ἀξίους ἑαυτοὺς πεποιηκότων οὐδενὸς σκυθρωποῦ ἀλλ' ἐφ'
ᾧ χαίρειν χρή. διὸ αὐτῶν ἐστι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον σὺν τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ κρίσει διακόνῳ
κεχρημένῃ. 10 ii 21–25 ὁ οὖν διδάσκων ἕτερον σεαυτὸν οὐ διδάσκεις; ὁ κηρύσσων μὴ
κλέπτειν κλέπτεις; ὁ λέγων μὴ μοιχεύειν μοιχεύεις; ὁ βδελυσσόμενος τὰ εἴδωλα
ἱεροσυλεῖς; ὃς ἐν νόμῳ καυχᾶσαι, διὰ τῆς παραβάσεως τοῦ νόμου τὸν θεὸν ἀτιμάζεις;
τὸ γὰρ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ δι' ὑμῶν βλασφημεῖται ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι καθὼς γέγραπται·
περιτομὴ μὲν γὰρ ὠφελεῖ, ἐὰν νόμον πράσσῃς· ἐὰν δὲ παραβάτης νόμου ᾖς, ἡ
περιτομή σου ἀκροβυστία γέγονεν. ζητῆσαι χρὴ ποσαχῶς ὁ νόμος λέγεται, καὶ
μάλιστα παρὰ τῷ ἀποστόλῳ, ἵνα μὴ δόξῃ ἐναντιοῦσθαι ἑαυτῷ· ποτὲ μὲν εἰ
περιτέμνε θε, Χρι τὸ ὑμᾶ οὐδὲν ὠφελή ει· ποτὲ δὲ περιτομὴν ὠφελεῖν ἐὰν νόμον τις
πράσσῃ. ἔστιν οὖν νόμος καθ' ἕνα τρόπον ψιλὸν τὸ Μωσέως γράμμα, καθ' ὃ
σημαινόμενον εἴρηται τὸ εἰ ἐν νόμῳ δικαιοῦ θε τῆ χάριτο ἐξεπέ ατε· καὶ τὸ ὁ νόμο
παιδαγωγὸ ἡμῶν γέγονεν εἰ Χρι τόν. ἔστι καὶ ὁ κατὰ πνεῦμα νόμος κυρίως
ὀνομαζόμενος, καθ' ὃ εἴρηται ὥ τε ὁ μὲν νόμο ἅγιο καὶ ἡ ἐντολὴ ἁγία. ἔστι καὶ ὁ
pass_a_gloss: Just as something lower was shown to be, so also God's wrath from heaven is upon us; another thing, however, is whether wrath comes from heaven but not from God. If God has revealed truth to all people through the reasoning in nature and made known the knowledge of himself as each has received when they completed the reasoning, then clearly there will be a judgment through all ungodly and unjust things—more for some, less for others—according to proportion, so that the revelation of God's wrath from heaven may come. To those who by perseverance in good work seek glory, honor, and immortality, eternal life; but to those from rivalry and who disobey the truth while following injustice, there is wrath and anger, distress and anguish upon every human soul doing evil, first the Jew and also the Greek. Wrath is the punishment following those who sin; anger they define as wrath stirred up and made known, and this anger has the function of convicting when someone suffers from sins, either their conscience being struck or troublesome things following sin. But affliction also follows such people, not the endurance producing it, nor if one fasting boasts, but only if bound together with distress. No one would be distressed if they had made their heart broad like a snake's width and heard the apostle say, 'Be widened, you also.' For evil things tend to gather and narrow the soul, as the devil hides in ambush according to the serpent. Glory, honor, and peace to everyone who does good, first the Jew and also the Greek, for there is no partiality with God. Therefore, the one who does good and valuable things, revealing their own worth, will receive honor by ascending through repentance, from which they fell having become like senseless beasts; and having understood the things worthy of immortality, they are raised up in glory to eternal life. And in peace is everyone who is undistracted and not drawn away by anything else to think or act contrary to the truth, according to how God's peace guards your hearts and thoughts in Christ Jesus, and may peace be multiplied to you, and I give you my peace; and the prophet also says that peace will be abundant in the Lord's visitation, so that false light, both day and night, may no longer exist. For those who sinned without law will also perish without law, and those who sinned under the law will be judged by the law; for not the hearers of the law are righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified. To be judged is according to law and through law, but to perish does not admit of law; nor does anyone else destroy them so that they may be judged by law of destruction, but destruction holds those who sinned without law. But those who sinned under the law, not having completely deserted it, either neglecting or being overcome, yet intending to live according to the law, will be judged by the law. With their conscience bearing witness and their thoughts accusing or excusing one another, on the day when God judges the secret things of people according to my gospel through Jesus Christ. [Or thus:] God judges according to the gospel, which is Paul's gospel, and those who have made themselves worthy like him, of whom there is no sorrowful person, but on which one should rejoice. Therefore, their gospel is with God's judgment as a minister entrusted with it. Therefore, the one who teaches another thing about themselves, do they not teach themselves? The one who preaches not to steal, do they steal? The one who says not to commit adultery, do they commit adultery? The one who abhors idols, do they rob temples? The one who boasts in the law, by transgressing the law, do they dishonor God? For the name of God is blasphemed among the nations as it is written. Circumcision indeed profits if you practice the law; but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision. One must seek how often the law is spoken, especially by the apostle, so as not to seem to contradict oneself; at times when one is circumcised, Christ does not benefit you at all; at other times, circumcision benefits if one practices the law. Thus the law is, in one sense, merely the letter of Moses; in its meaning, it has been said that if one is justified by the law, it is by grace that they have surpassed; and the law has become our pedagogue until Christ. pass_b_english: Just as what is lower has been revealed, so too does divine wrath from heaven rest upon us—though one might ask whether this wrath comes from heaven but not from God. If God has made truth known to all through the reasoning found in nature, and has revealed himself to each according to their capacity to complete that reasoning, then judgment must follow upon all ungodly and unjust deeds—more heavily for some, less for others—in proportion, so that the revelation of God’s heavenly wrath may be fulfilled. To those who, through steadfastness in good works, pursue glory, honor, and immortality, eternal life is given; but to those driven by rivalry, who reject truth while embracing injustice, wrath and anger, distress and anguish come upon every soul that does evil—first the Jew, then the Greek. Wrath is the punishment that follows sin; anger, they say, is wrath roused and made manifest, serving to convict when one suffers from sin—either through conscience being struck or through troubles that follow sin. Yet distress also follows such people, not from endurance itself, nor from fasting done for show, but only when it is bound up with anguish. No one would feel straitened if they had widened their heart like a snake’s girth and heard the apostle say, ‘Be widened, you also.’ For evil things tend to gather and narrow the soul, as the devil lies in ambush like a serpent. Glory, honor, and peace belong to everyone who does good—first the Jew, then the Greek—for God shows no partiality. Thus, the one who does good and valuable deeds, revealing their own worth, will receive honor by rising through repentance, from which they fell having become like senseless beasts; and having grasped what is worthy of immortality, they are raised in glory to eternal life. And in peace is everyone who is undistracted, not drawn aside by anything else to think or act against the truth, according to how God’s peace guards your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus—may peace be multiplied to you, and I give you my peace; and the prophet declares that peace will abound in the Lord’s visitation, so that false light, both by day and night, may cease to exist. For those who sinned without law will also perish without law, and those who sinned under the law will be judged by the law; for it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but the doers who will be justified. Judgment comes according to law and through law, but destruction does not submit to law—nor does anyone else destroy them so that they may be judged by a law of destruction, but destruction holds those who sinned without law. Yet those who sinned under the law, not having utterly deserted it, whether by neglect or being overcome, yet still intending to live by it, will be judged by the law. With their conscience bearing witness and their thoughts accusing or excusing one another, on the day when God judges the secrets of humanity according to my gospel through Jesus Christ. [Or thus:] God judges according to the gospel, which is Paul’s gospel, and those who have made themselves worthy like him—among whom there is no sorrowful person, but only cause for joy—thus their gospel stands with God’s judgment as a minister entrusted with it. Therefore, the one who teaches something else about themselves, do they not teach themselves? The one who preaches against stealing, do they steal? The one who says not to commit adultery, do they commit adultery? The one who abhors idols, do they rob temples? The one who boasts in the law, yet transgresses it, do they dishonor God? For the name of God is blasphemed among the nations as it is written. Circumcision profits if you keep the law; but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision. One must inquire how often the law is spoken, especially by the apostle, so as not to appear to contradict oneself; at times when one is circumcised, Christ does not benefit you at all; at other times, circumcision helps if one practices the law. choices.issue: Whether divine wrath originates from heaven but not from God
choices.choice: The text raises the question but does not resolve it, leaving open whether wrath comes from heaven without being directly from God.

choices.issue: The role of conscience in moral judgment
choices.choice: Conscience bears witness and either accuses or excuses individuals, functioning as an internal guide on the day of divine judgment.
